name: Page tools for AI agents (WebMCP)
plain: A page can list actions an AI agent in the browser may call, instead of the agent guessing at buttons.
meaning: WebMCP is a proposed web standard. A page registers named tools with a description and input schema through navigator.modelContext, or marks up forms. A browser agent can then call a tool such as search flights or add to cart directly. It is an early preview in Chrome behind a flag and may change.

web.api: navigator.modelContext.registerTool({name, description, inputSchema, execute}); declarative form attributes

access.prompt_ui: None defined yet in the draft
access.persistence: Tools live while the page is open
access.revocation: Close the page or unregister the tool
access.iframe: Draft rules for frames are not settled
steps: Page registers tools with names and input schemas
An agent in the browser reads the tool list
The agent calls a tool; the page code runs it
Browser rules for who may call tools are still being drafted

chrome.note: Early preview behind a flag; may change

fields.name: description
fields.range: what the tool does, read by the agent

fields.name: execute
fields.range: page code that runs when the agent calls the tool

limits.headline: Lets a site give an agent a clean, named list of actions
limits.user_action: None for the page owner. Agents or browsers may ask you before they call a tool
can: Expose named actions with typed inputs
Let an agent skip fragile clicking
Keep your own checks and limits in your tool code
Work next to the normal page for people
cannot: Run without a browser agent present
Stop an agent from using the visible page
limits.reach_label: A tool list on one page
limits.differs: Only Chrome has an early preview, behind a flag. Names, shapes and permission rules can still change.

story.what_it_is: A site tells agents what they can do, in a menu, rather than letting them poke at the screen.

marketing.vendor: W3C Web Machine Learning Community Group
marketing.name: WebMCP
marketing.pitch: Draft spec for exposing page tools to agents through the browser.

story.for_you: You will not see it. If you use a browser agent, the sites it visits may offer tools so the agent works faster and makes fewer mistakes.
story.for_makers: Validate every argument in your tool code and apply the same rules as for a user. Do not treat an agent call as safe. Plan for the spec to change.

use_cases.example: A store exposes add to cart and check stock as tools.
A travel site exposes a search flights tool that returns structured results.
A task app exposes create task and list tasks.
A team tests how agents use their tools in Chrome with the flag on.
An internal portal publishes approved actions for staff agents.
Clear tool names help agents act for people who cannot use a mouse.

risks: Agents acting without a clear person's yes

technical_bounds: Not identity; says nothing about who the agent is

legit_uses: Faster, safer agent actions than clicking
abuse: Agents doing more than the person meant

history.change: WebMCP early preview in Chrome behind a flag
